scope: Fix the overflow-clipped desktop splitter hit area and exercise actual pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture lifecycles. The overall C acceptance remains OPEN.

finding.reproduction: The 8px separator was positioned 4px outside its parent dock (left right:-4px, right left:-4px). Because .dock clips overflow, the separator center hit-tested the dock instead of the button; half of each target was inaccessible to pointer input.
finding.fix: Keep the complete 8px hit target inside each dock (left right:0, right left:0) and cache-bust editor.css in the editor index.
finding.regression_test: The real Chromium test proves both separators are fully inside their clipped parent and receive input at 1025, 1280 and 1920 CSS px; it then performs a genuine mouse drag/pointerup and verifies pointercancel and lostpointercapture retain/persist the last width and clear interaction state.
preserved_contracts: workspace widths persist in local shell state

implementation.reuse_review: The existing project-owned vanilla CSS shell, WAI-ARIA separator controls and Playwright Chromium fixture were reused. No external runtime code, new dependency, or infrastructure was needed.
